player.seasonOutlook: Baseball's greatest historical two-way player could be primed for his best season yet. On offense in 2025, Ohtani exceeded 50 home runs for a second consecutive season and stole 20-plus bases for a third straight year. On the mound, the Dodgers were uber-conservative with his recovery from his September 2023 elbow reconstruction, but Ohtani delivered per-start numbers in line with his pre-injury rates. His pitching usage also ramped up right in time for the playoffs, during which he became the first player in history to hit three home runs while also striking out 10 batters in one game in the Dodgers' NLCS clincher, triggering memories of his 2022, when he scored 411 fantasy points as a hitter and 475 as a pitcher. As the Dodgers surely will, so must you manage his daily utility -- he can be used as a DH or pitcher, but not both --  but Ohtani's potential puts him head and shoulders ahead of the pack.
